interests: I am interested in world models for generalizable robotic planning: how predictions of the physical world can support reliable action in unfamiliar environments.

My work develops the perceptual and predictive foundations for this goal, from recovering and retaining spatial evidence to imagining physically plausible 4D futures that guide robot actions and support pre-execution consistency checks.
My recent world–action model is evaluated through zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

I am now interested in agent–world model co-evolution: using task-relevant prediction errors to guide interaction and model refinement, while action-conditioned world models support policy evaluation, improvement, and longer-horizon planning.

papers.summary: S4NDBOX bridges visual imagination and robot control through explicit 4D futures, improving physical plausibility (+11.2% relative spatiotemporal IoU vs. RGB-only) and enabling pre-execution geometric verification (observed +7.9 pp success within three attempts vs. random ordering). OOD generalization over RGB-only: +13.3 pp success on RoboTwin Hard (clean-only training); +40.0 task-score points on single-view zero-shot sim-to-real settings.
